gap: No result ChatGPT got says that on the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 only the USB-C2 port runs a Starlink Mini: USB-C2 lists a 20V⎓5A profile (140 W max), while USB-C1 shares a 20 W cap with USB-A, so the wrong port fails Starlink's 100 W (20V/5A) minimum.
standout_why: Rivals checked: the three cited Starlink Help Center articles (a7fe6525 'How can I power my Starlink Mini?' and fba85643 'What USB power rating do I need', in its ws and gb copies), plus two results ChatGPT got but did not cite: the Mini spec sheet and the Mini accessories guide PDF. Limit: the Help Center articles render only in JavaScript and would not open for me through either the direct URL or a reader proxy. My view of what they say comes from Starlink's spec sheet and accessories guide, which I did open. Those Starlink documents state the requirement only for the dish side: 100 W at 20V/5A minimum with Starlink's USB-C to Barrel Jack cable, a 12–48 V 60 W DC input, a 5 m USB-C cable, and a Car Adapter for 12–24 V outlets. None of them says which port on a given power station meets the requirement. ChatGPT's own table stops at '140W charger: supported if the port provides 20V/5A'. No result covers the Anker port split (C1 limited to 20 W), the RIVER 3 Plus's single USB-C port at exactly 20V⎓5A and 100 W, or the fact that these stations' 12 V car outlets can run the Mini through the Car Adapter.
decides: This confirms that both the Anker C1000 Gen 2 and the EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus can run the Mini over USB-C, with conditions. On the Anker the cable must go into USB-C2. The RIVER 3 Plus meets 20V⎓5A exactly, with no wattage to spare and only one USB-C port. Each also has a 12 V car outlet rated 120–126 W, above the Mini's 60 W input rating. That outlet plus Starlink's Mini Car Adapter is a second route that doesn't depend on USB-C profiles. The page's USB-C column should therefore name the qualifying port rather than the station's total USB-C wattage. The BLUETTI rows stay unconfirmed until their port profiles are sourced.

findings.label: Starlink Mini USB PD requirement
findings.value: 100 W, 20V/5A minimum (with Starlink USB-C to Barrel Jack Cable Accessory)
findings.note: Opened through the r.jina.ai reader because the direct PDF fetch returned compressed streams. Quoted as written. The requirement is tied to Starlink's own USB-C to barrel cable.

findings.label: Starlink Mini DC input rating and average draw
findings.value: Input 12–48 V, 60 W; average consumption 25–40 W
findings.note: Lines quoted from the spec sheet: 'Input Rating 12-48V 60W' and 'Power Consumption Average: 25-40W'. The kit's power supply is rated 100–240 V ~ 1.6 A, 50–60 Hz.

findings.label: Length, required source, and an exclusion
findings.value: 5 m (16.4 ft); requires a 100 W (20V/5A) power source; 'not suitable for charging devices like cellphones'
findings.note: Opened through the r.jina.ai reader. The phone exclusion is Starlink's own wording, so the cable is one-way: power source to Mini only.

findings.label: Compatible outlets and kit contents
findings.value: Works with any standard automotive 12–24 V auxiliary power outlet; the kit contains the Mini Car Adapter and the Mini USB-C Cable; it replaces the Mini 15 m Power Cable and Mini Power Supply
findings.note: Listed compatibility: Starlink Mini. Package 208.5 × 153.75 × 67.5 mm, 0.43 kg. The reader flagged that some DC-cable blocks in this PDF extracted out of order. The Car Adapter and USB-C cable blocks read cleanly.

findings.label: USB-C2 output profiles
findings.note: From the maker's US spec list. The page prints '5V~ 3V', which looks like a typo for 3A. The listed 20V 5A profile = 100 W, which meets Starlink's minimum.

findings.label: USB-C1 shared cap (exclusion)
findings.value: USB-A and USB-C1 total 20 W max
findings.note: 20 W is far below Starlink's 100 W (20V/5A) minimum, so USB-C1 cannot run the Mini. Use USB-C2.

findings.label: Car outlet rating
findings.note: 12 V falls within the Car Adapter's 12–24 V outlet range and the Mini's 12–48 V input. 120 W is above the Mini's 60 W input rating (120 ≥ 60). This route through the Starlink Car Adapter is an inference from the two maker documents. Neither maker tested this pairing.

findings.label: USB-C output
findings.source_title: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-02-12)
findings.note: This is StorageReview's spec table, not a measurement. The EcoFlow US product URLs I tried returned 404 or 429. 20V × 5A = 100 W, exactly Starlink's minimum, with no wattage to spare and only one USB-C port.

findings.label: Car output
findings.source_title: EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus Review (StorageReview, Dylan Dougherty, 2025-02-12)
findings.note: 12.6 V falls within the Car Adapter's 12–24 V range and 126 W exceeds the Mini's 60 W input rating. This is an inference, not a tested pairing.

findings.label: USB-C headline output and price
findings.value: One USB-C port with PD 3.1, up to 140 W; $299.99 at bluettipower.com
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Elite 30 V2 Portable Power Station | 600W 288Wh
findings.note: The 140 W line comes from the maker page, opened through the reader. The price comes from the store's Shopify data via storecheck. The Blush Pink listing shows $289.99. The page does not list per-voltage PD profiles, so I have not confirmed a 20V/5A profile.
